original_question:
A function ψ on R^n is r-regular for r = 0,1,2,… or ∞ if ψ is C^r and all partial derivatives up to order r decay polynomially: ∂^α ψ(x) = O(|x|^{−N}) as |x|→∞ for all |α| ≤ r, for some N>0.

Does there exist an ∞-regular wavelet construction in higher dimensions?
target_in_paper: Section 3.5, Problem 3.5: the paper’s formal version of your draft is the Schwartz-class/∞-regular existence problem for integer expansive dilations with lattice Γ=Z^n, motivated by the end of Section 3.4 where the authors recall r-regularity and say that the existence of ∞-regular wavelets in higher dimensions is still open. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the local cue that identifies the problem: it reproduces the paper’s notion of r-regularity closely and focuses on the higher-dimensional existence of ∞-regular wavelets. That is exactly the issue the paper isolates at the end of Section 3.4 before restating it in Section 3.5 as a Schwartz-class wavelet problem. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is not asking about arbitrary higher-dimensional wavelets; it asks about wavelets associated with an integer expansive dilation A and the standard lattice Γ=Z^n. Here 'integer expansive' means A∈GL_n(R), A Z^n⊂Z^n (equivalently, A has integer entries), and every eigenvalue λ of A satisfies |λ|>1. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))

In the paper, 'wavelet' is used in the affine-system sense of Definition 3.1, and in higher dimensions it may be a finite family Ψ={ψ^1,…,ψ^L} rather than a single generator. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))

The orthonormality condition is missing: the affine system { |det A|^{j/2} ψ^l(A^j x-k) : l=1,…,L, j∈Z, k∈Z^n } must form an orthonormal basis of L^2(R^n). ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))

The paper explicitly translates the ∞-regular formulation into Schwartz-class language: Section 3.5 says that Schwartz class is the collection of all ∞-regular functions on R^n. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))

Your phrase 'in higher dimensions' is too vague for the paper’s exact intent. Because the one-dimensional case is classical and Theorem 3.7 settles every expansive 2×2 integer dilation, the unresolved range is really n≥3. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))

The quantifier is not explicit. The paper’s problem is naturally read as: given an expansive integer dilation A (equivalently, for each such A), does there exist such a wavelet associated with (A,Z^n)? It is not merely asking whether some higher-dimensional example exists. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))

Nearby context adds a hidden restriction once multiple generators are allowed: for a well-localized orthonormal wavelet associated with an integer dilation, the number L of generators must be divisible by |det A|-1. Your draft omits this paper-relevant constraint. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
refined_question: Let n≥3 and let A∈GL_n(R) be an expansive integer dilation, i.e. A Z^n⊂Z^n and every eigenvalue λ of A satisfies |λ|>1. Does there exist a finite family Ψ={ψ^1,…,ψ^L}⊂S(R^n) (equivalently, each ψ^l is ∞-regular), for some finite L (necessarily divisible by |det A|-1), such that the affine system { |det A|^{j/2} ψ^l(A^j x-k) : l=1,…,L, j∈Z, k∈Z^n } is an orthonormal basis of L^2(R^n)? ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent official formulation from the paper: Do Schwartz class wavelets exist for integer expansive dilations A and lattice Γ=Z^n? ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
justification: The draft is not aiming at the full breadth of Problem 3.4; it is aiming at the narrower ∞-regular specialization that the authors immediately single out at the end of Section 3.4 and then formalize in Section 3.5. The paper first recalls Meyer’s definition of r-regularity, then states that the existence of ∞-regular wavelets in higher dimensions is still open, then identifies Schwartz class with ∞-regularity, and finally poses Problem 3.5 for integer expansive dilations and Γ=Z^n. Definition 3.1 supplies the missing affine-basis meaning of 'wavelet', and Theorem 3.7 shows why the unresolved part starts only in dimension 3. ([pages.uoregon.edu](https://pages.uoregon.edu/mbownik/preprints/open.pdf))
